title: Towards Enriched Controllability for Educational Question Generation
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of improving controllability in educational question generation (QG), specifically whether a model can be guided to produce questions of a desired explicitness level. The authors argue that educational QG can better support teaching and learning if teachers or systems can control question properties such as whether a question is explicit or implicit, and whether it targets certain narrative elements in a story.

The study fine-tunes T5-based QG models on the FairytaleQA dataset, which contains question-answer pairs derived from children-friendly stories. The proposed control mechanism adds special tokens to the input to condition generation on question explicitness alone, on narrative element alone, or on both simultaneously. The paper compares these controlled models with a baseline that does not include the control attribute, using automatic metrics on a reorganized controlled test set.

The dataset and context are educational narrative comprehension questions from children’s stories, but the paper is a machine learning methods study rather than a learner experiment. The main finding is that explicitness control is effective for influencing the kind of answer required and that narrative-element control more strongly changes the surface form of generated questions. The authors conclude that simultaneous control of explicitness and narrative elements is feasible and useful for enriched controllability in educational QG, while noting that future work should include large-scale human evaluation in authentic educational settings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed empirical NLP paper, but it is not a learner-impact study and does not use an RCT or quasi-experimental design in educational settings. Evidence is based on automatic metrics over a dataset rather than direct classroom outcomes, so credibility for educational impact is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows modest to strong improvements in text-generation metrics for controlled question generation, especially for narrative control, but these are proxy outcomes rather than student learning gains. No direct educational impact or user study is reported, so real-world impact remains unclear.

interventions.use_case: controllable automated educational question generation from children-friendly stories using a fine-tuned T5 text-to-text model with prompts for explicitness and narrative element control

finding.finding_summary: The paper evaluates educational question generation quality for reading-comprehension practice using automatic metrics on FairytaleQA. In the controlled test, explicitness control with the ex-section:question-answer model improved QA answerability for explicit questions (ROUGE-L F1=0.741, EXACT MATCH=0.483) versus implicit questions (ROUGE-L F1=0.431, EXACT MATCH=0.306), and the combined nar-ex model further improved implicit QA performance (ROUGE-L F1=0.514, EXACT MATCH=0.343). For QG, narrative control substantially improved generated-question similarity to gold questions (ROUGE-L F1=0.432, BLEU-4=0.189-0.195, BLEURT=0.424-0.432) compared with the section-only baseline (ROUGE-L F1=0.305, BLEU-4=0.099, BLEURT=0.370).
finding.measure: ROUGE-L F1, EXACT MATCH, BLEU-4, BLEURT on question generation/answering for reading-comprehension questions
finding.study_size: n=1007 test QA pairs (controlled test derived from the FairytaleQA test split); dataset overall n=10,580 QA pairs from 278 stories
